newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank reform bill introduced in House.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank reform bill introduced in House.

text.p: A financial modernization bill that would let banks sell some securities, including municipal revenue bonds, was introduced Wednesday by Rep. Marge Roukema, R-New Jersey.
Roukema, who chairs a House Banking subcommittee, said the legisation would not be considered until after the next session of Congress begins in January.

"This represensents the first step toward crafting meaningful financial reform legislation that will take us into the 21st century and put us on sound footing to compete in the global marketplace," Roukema said at a news conference.

Roukema said the bill would require the conversion of thrift institutions to banks by January 1, 1998 as part of a long-term plan to solve the financial problems of the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
The bill would also allow financial companies to affiliate with banks.

Roukema said supporters of the bill included the American Bankers Association, the Investment Company Institute and the Securities Industry Association. She said she would seek discussions with the insurance industry on the bill.
